title: Supported Bluetooth Blood Glucose Meters?
body: Is there a complete list of all supported bluetooth blood glucose meters? I know that the Conture Next One and the OneTouch Select Plus Flex is compatible, but both use CR2032 Batteries and I hvae to replace it too often. I search for something with a LiON accu and a MicroUSB or USB-C Charging port. This is these days better to find than a pack of coincells. The Libre Freestyle 2 Reader does take bloodsugar tests and recharges over USB, but don't  exports the data via bluetooth, right?

comments.body: Does the breuer gl 50 evo reader is supported by xdrip?
@tremor Battery for Contour One lasts for about a year... Mine is currently on 14 months...
@andyrozman With automatic bluetooth connection to xDrip?
Yes @tremor.  The Contour Next One connects to xDrip+ via Bluetooth. You have to set options for what to do with the automatically transferred readings.

@tremor Would you please close this issue if your question has been answered?
There are currently 2 support channels you can use for asking questions.
https://www.facebook.com/groups/xDripG5
https://gitter.im/jamorham/xDrip-plus
We will hopefully be able to add some documentation as well later.
Thanks

xDrip implements the Generic Attribute Profile (GATT) for blood glucose meters (BGM), at least partially. Hence, every BGM should be supported if they implement the BGM GATT as well - so far the theory. In practice, not every BGM implementing this GATT works as expected. For instance, the [FORA 6 Connect](https://foracare.com/multi-functional-monitoring-system/6-connect-multi-functional-monitoring-system) does not work, but I'm working on supporting it.

@JasonJShuler If there is a reason you don't like the two mentioned platforms for having a conversation, I can offer you a third choice:
https://github.com/Navid200/xDrip/discussions
